comments.text:
Regarding scale, the advantage to having a million little pieces like you mentioned is for the OTHER thing you mentioned you do when you see a trending article: you look for other stories to verify it.

If a bad actor can get one story out, they could for sure get out multiple variations of that story. Suddenly, you’ve got multiple different sources talking about this from multiple places on the net. How do you verify your source if every place you go also has some variation of the same story? It becomes more believable when we see it multiple places. That’s the danger, I think.

comments.author: @chrisanderson7820
comments.text: Propaganda is often about volume, the whole "tell a lie enough times and it becomes truth". So what AI does is it democratizes effort (ironically). In the past if you wanted to make a fake you'd need a trained graphic artist to take time to create 1 false image in Photoshop, then that 1 image could be debunked by 10 other experts. Now you can have a million randos in their basement (or bot farms) creating 1,000 fake images each and now you have an uncheckable tsunami of fakes. Often the objective is not to have you believe a particular image but instead to so thoroughly muddy the waters of reality that you end up distrusting EVERYTHING. "I can't tell who said what so I'm just not going to vote" etc.

comments.author: @anckrnews
comments.text: These speculations about simulations are a fascinating philosophical exercise, but care should be taken to make sure that people don’t misinterpret any of this as anything beyond philosophical speculation. The presentation of this topic in this video and the interview segment that was shown make no qualifications about this, and present it in a very matter-of-fact fashion. This could have the effect of misleading people into thinking that there is some scientific basis for suspecting any of this. There is none at this time, not from physics and not from AI research. The concept that is discussed in this clip, if true, would invalidate all know physics, and all known principles of thermodynamics. It would require an extraordinary amount of evidence to justify that. The idea of ‘free energy’ has been the focus of many misleading pseudoscientific endeavors throughout history. To so blithely treat this as a serious scientific subject, honestly calls into question the credibility of everyone in this video. To reiterate, it’s a perfectly valid and valuable philosophical topic, but without even presenting a model for how you could test for any of this in the empirical universe, it’s not actually much more intellectually rigorous than dorm room philosophy. I am very excited about the potential of AI technology, but when I hear smart people in that field stepping out of their lane like this, I start to worry about how much of this is actually tech bro smoke and mirrors. I don’t think it is, but advocates for the industry need to be held to a higher standard than what this video presents.
